# PicoCalc Space Game

*README.MD file mostly generated by Anthropic's Claude AI because Thomas Dzubin hates documenting code.  LOL*

A parallax starfield with a steerable ship, for the [ClockworkPi
PicoCalc](https://www.clockworkpi.com/picocalc), built on the Raspberry Pi Pico
SDK and the driver set from
[picocalc-text-starter](https://github.com/BlairLeduc/picocalc-text-starter) by
Blair Leduc.

Red alien squares hunt you across a wrapping, 10,000-pixel-wide universe;
shoot them, dodge them, out-manoeuvre them into each other, and don't run out
of fuel. It's still a sketch - no waves - but there's a fail state, a kill
counter, and a title + **four-level difficulty pick** on startup.

## Startup

**Before every game** - the first one and every restart after `GAME OVER` - one
**start screen** shows the big blocky title (*YET ANOTHER SPACE ALIEN GAME
(YASAG)*, then a `V1.00A  by Thomas Dzubin` line - there's no large font, so the
8x10 one is just drawn scaled up) with the difficulty choice on the lines below
it. The very first showing (program startup) plays a short happy jingle. Press a
number to pick and go:

| Key | Label | Count | Aliens |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | *No aliens* | 0 | None at all - just your ship in an empty universe. Two **hints**: `Arrow Keys to Move` at the start, `Press Q to Quit` at the 1- and 2-minute marks |
| **1** | *Easy Aliens (with hints)* | 20 | Spawn, but never move or hunt. Still shootable and still deadly to fly into. On-screen **hints** (grey text + arrow) show which keys move and fire, point you at the next alien, and nag you to raise shields |
| **2** | *Regular Aliens* | 40 | Hunt once they see you - **the normal game** |
| **3** | *Hard Aliens* | 60 | All of them hunt you at once, wherever they are (a cloak still hides you); torpedoes come twice as fast as levels 1-2 |

Your pick shows as **`Lv N`** in the right strip, just above the kill counter.

Then a **`CONTROLS`** screen lists the key map with a **10-second countdown**
along the bottom. The game starts when the countdown hits `0`, or the moment
you press any key - except **`ESC`**, which goes back to the start screen.

`~` reboots to BOOTSEL (for reflashing) from anywhere.

## What you see

- A **304 x 228 play box** (a 4:3 rectangle, like an old TV) in the top-left
  corner of the 320 x 320 LCD, drawn with a **3-pixel border**.
- A **random starfield** inside the box. Every star has its own **depth**: near
  stars are bright and sweep past fast, far stars are dim blue-grey and barely
  move. That continuous spread of speeds is the parallax. Get moving fast and
  the near stars **stretch into streaks** - that is what sells the speed.
- A small white **filled triangle ship**, always parked at the centre of the
  box. Only its heading changes - the world moves around it. It turns **yellow**
  once hull damage passes **33%** *or* power drops below **33%** (a "wounded"
  warning), and **cyan** while the shield is up (which wins over the yellow).
- A big **orange flame** off the ship's tail for about a second after each `Up`
  press, flickering in length and shade every frame, then gone - thrust is a
  burst, not a hold.
- **Two small white flames** off the front sides for about a second after each
  `Down` press - the retro-brake slowing you down.
- A **small white attitude jet** off one front side while you hold `Left` or
  `Right` - it fires on the side *opposite* the turn, so its push swings the
  nose the way you asked.
- **Green torpedo tracers** from the nose (opposite the flame) when you press
  `Space` - up to 20 at a time, each flying straight to the box edge and
  winking out. They move faster than the ship can ever travel, so you can never
  fly into your own fire.
- **White torpedo tracers** coming the other way - fired *at* you by a shooter
  alien (see below). Slower than your fire, and each one flies a dead-straight
  line, so nudging the ship forward or back after it's fired slips the shot; the
  shield stops them too. (They used to be red, but red was near-invisible on the
  PicoCalc LCD.)
- When the **shield** is up (`S`), the hull turns cyan and a cyan hex
  ring is drawn around the ship. Its level shows on its own gauge (below).
- **Solid alien squares**, roughly the ship's size, drifting on random headings
  until one wanders into view - then it locks on and charges you. They're
  **red** at full health; one player-torpedo hit leaves a square **yellow**
  ("wounded"), a second destroys it (flash bright white and vanish). A hit from
  another alien kills instantly. About **1 in 4** sits still and shoots at you
  instead.
- Five short **gauges** stacked flush (no gap) in the strip below the box - a
  green **fuel** bar, a purple **power** bar, an amber **ammo** bar, a cyan
  **shield** bar and a red **damage** bar (top to bottom). Fuel, power, shield
  and damage read as a bare **`Fuel  94%`** / **`Power 100%`** / **`Shields  60%`**
  / **`Damage  20%`** (the damage bar *fills* as you get hurt); ammo keeps its
  count, **`Ammo 285/300`**.
- To the right of those readouts, a small column: **`Lv N`** (chosen
  difficulty) with a **`MM:SS` countdown clock** beside it - it **starts at
  `15:00` and ticks down**, pauses when the game does, and at **`00:00` the game
  is over** (on every level). A **`Kills NN/MM`**
  counter (aliens removed out of the total that will ever appear - **20** on
  level 1, **40** on level 2, **60** on level 3; **`No Aliens`** instead at
  difficulty 0), and **`CLOAKED`** while cloaked.
- Your **universal coordinates** (`X:##### Y:#####`) in the bottom-right
  corner - where the ship is on the big fixed grid the whole game lives on.
- **Long Range Sensors** - small red triangular blips just inside the box
  edges, pointing at off-screen aliens that line up straight above / below /
  left / right of the box. (Diagonally-off aliens don't show.)

The starfield scrolls opposite to the ship's velocity, so it can drift
horizontally, vertically or diagonally. A star that slides off one edge is
wrapped to the opposite edge with a fresh random position **and a fresh depth**,
so the field never visibly repeats.

The ship has **real inertia and no drag** - in vacuum it coasts. Velocity is a
**vector**: each `Up` press adds a shove along the way the nose points *to what
you already have*, so if you thrust, turn, and thrust again your new course is
the sum of the pushes - and its length is your speed (capped at a maximum).

`Down` is the exact **mirror of `Up`**: one push per press along the *opposite*
of the nose, at **half the strength**. It is **not a brake** - from a dead stop,
tapping `Down` flies you backwards at half the up-thrust rate.

Nothing is a dedicated "slow down." Your **nose** (heading) and your
**trajectory** (which way you're actually drifting - watch the starfield, it
scrolls the *opposite* way) are separate things. `Up` always pushes toward the
nose; `Down` always pushes out the front. To lose speed you point a push
*against* your drift:

- point the nose the **same way you're drifting**, tap `Down`; **or**
- point the nose **backwards along your drift** (retrograde), tap `Up`.

Either adds a vector that partly cancels your velocity; enough taps and you
stop. (Nose *along* your drift + `Up` is the opposite - that speeds you up.)

Rotation is **orientation only** - turning the ship does *not* bend the course
you are already on. So you can be flying one way while facing another, coasting
sideways past the stars.

### Flip and burn (`Enter`)

`Enter` fires off a **flip-and-burn**, straight out of *The Expanse*: the ship
takes over, swings itself around until the nose points **retrograde** (main
engine aimed the way you're travelling), then burns the main engine until you're
**completely stopped**. However fast you were going, however you were pointed,
`Enter` always leaves you dead in space. It needs fuel and some actual speed to
do anything.

It **is** an autopilot, so it shares the one autopilot banner: while it runs
your steering, thrust and cloak keys do nothing (you can still shoot) and the
banner near the top of the box reads **`AUTOPILOT`** / **`flip-and-burn`**. When
it finishes the banner drops back to whatever mode you were in - `AUTOPILOT` if
autopilot was on, otherwise a brief `MANUAL` flash. It isn't instant: the flip
alone can take a second or two, during which an alien can close the distance and
ram you, or you can drift into one. Commit carefully.

## Gauges

Five short bars stacked **flush** below the box - **fuel**, **power**, **ammo**,
**shield**, **damage** - each shown two ways at once (for the graphic-gauge
crowd and the text-gauge crowd both): a coloured bar, and a readout beside it.
Fuel / power / shield / damage read as a bare percentage (`Fuel  94%`,
`Power 100%`, `Shields  60%`, `Damage  20%`); the fuel/power/ammo/shield bars
*drain* left-to-right as they're spent, the damage bar *fills* as you take
hits. Ammo keeps its `cur/max` count. The `Lv` / `Kills` / `CLOAKED` readouts
sit in a column just right of those numbers.

**Fuel** (green) - every manoeuvre spends it:

- Starts at **500**.
- Each **distinct** `Up` (forward) press costs **2**; each **distinct** `Down`
  (reverse) press costs **1** - holding the key does nothing, so you can't drain
  the tank by leaning on it.
- Turning with `Left` / `Right` costs fuel by **time held** - about **5 a
  second** while the ship is actually rotating (roughly 4-5 for a 90 degree
  turn), charged the same way whether you tap or hold. A flip-and-burn's flip
  pays at the same rate.
- **At 0 you're dead in space** - `Up`, `Down` *and* `Left`/`Right` all stop
  responding. No forward or reverse thrust, no turning; you just coast on
  whatever velocity you had.

**Power** (purple) - feeds the shield and the cloak:

- Starts at **300**.
- Raising the shield (`S`) spends **20**, once. The cloak drains **2 a second**.
- No recharge - below **20** you can't raise the shield again, and **at 0 the
  game is over** (life support needs power). Below **33%** the ship's hull goes
  **yellow** (same "wounded" warning as high hull damage).

**Ammo** (amber) - one round per shot:

- Starts at **300**.
- Each torpedo that actually leaves the nose costs **1** (a shot that's dropped
  because all 20 on-screen slots are full doesn't count).
- **At 0, `Space` does nothing.**

**Shield** (cyan) - the 0-100% shield level (see below).

Fuel, power and ammo never refill. There's no speed readout - watch the
starfield.

### Shield

The shield is a **0-100% level** on its own cyan gauge. Press `S` and it jumps
to **100%** (costs 20 power - so you can't raise it without that much power);
press `S` again to drop it. It has no timer - it only goes **down**, by damage:

- an **alien torpedo** that hits it: **-1%** (the torpedo is stopped).
- an **alien that rams** you: **-20%** (the alien still dies).

At **0%** the shield is down, and further hits go straight to the hull as
**damage** (below). Cloaking drops the shield too.

### Damage

Separate from the shield, the hull carries a **0-100% damage** meter (its own
red gauge, which *fills* as it rises), starting at **0**. It only climbs while
the **shield is down**:

- an **alien torpedo** through the hull: **+10%**.
- an **alien ramming** you: **+40%** (the alien is wrecked in the crash too).

Past **33%** damage (or with power below **33%**) the ship's hull is drawn
**yellow** ("wounded") - unless the shield is up, which shows cyan regardless.
The crew slowly patches things up - **-1% every two seconds**. Hit **100%** and
the rocket is destroyed.

## The universe

The whole game sits on one fixed pixel grid, **10,000 pixels on a side** (stored
as 32-bit integers - the type could hold a grid a billion pixels a side). The
ship never
actually moves on screen - it's pinned to the centre of the box - so what
changes is *where on that grid* it is. Every frame it steps by the velocity
vector; the starfield scrolls the other way to show it.

You start in the **exact middle** (`5000, 5000`). The grid **wraps** - run far
enough in any direction and the coordinate rolls back around. The live
`X:##### Y:#####` readout sits in the bottom-right corner.

Alien ships carry their own grid coordinate; where one shows on your screen is
just its position minus yours, offset from the box centre.

## Aliens

Squares about the size of your ship, **red** at full health. Each spawns **200
to 1000 pixels** away (always just off-screen, never right on top of you) and
drifts off on its **own random heading** - it isn't aiming at you yet. The
moment its square touches the play box it's *seen* you: it **stops dead for a
beat, then turns and charges straight at you**, and from then on it never lets
go. They move at **the slowest speed your own rocket can go**, so you can always
outrun one - but keep flying and more keep coming. Up to 8 are in play at once;
**20 / 40 / 60** will appear over a level-1 / level-2 / level-3 game. A drifter
that never spots you and wanders far off is quietly swapped for a new one.

That's the **level 2** behaviour described here and below. **Level 1** skips all
of it - the squares just sit where they spawn (still shootable, still fatal to
ram). **Level 3** skips the drift-and-spot - every alien charges you from the
moment it exists, wherever it is in the universe. **Level 0** spawns none.

### Hints (difficulty 0 and 1 only)

The two "with hints" difficulties - **level 0** (`No aliens`) and **level 1**
(`Easy Aliens (with hints)`) - show **hints**: big **grey** text along the
bottom of the box, each for **two seconds**.

- **`Arrow Keys to Move`** - once, as the game starts. **Levels 0 and 1.**
- **`Press Q to Quit`** - at the **1-minute** and **2-minute** marks. **Level 0
  only** (there's nothing else to do there).
- **`Next Alien This Way`** *(level 1)* - whenever the play box is clear of
  aliens but some are still out there, plus a grey arrow whose point aims at the
  nearest off-screen one. It also pops up when a **flip-and-burn** finishes with
  the box still empty. Fly the way it points.
- **`Use S for Shields`** *(level 1)* - the moment your hull turns yellow
  ("wounded" - from hull damage or low power) while the shield is down.
- **`SPACE key to fire`** *(level 1)* - once, if you're **30 seconds** into the
  game and still haven't fired a single torpedo.

(Only one line shows at a time; priority is move > next-alien arrow > shields >
fire > quit.)

**Alien health.** Each alien has its own **0-100% damage** meter. One of your
torpedoes does **60%**, so it takes **two hits** to destroy one. After the first
hit the square turns **yellow** ("wounded"); its crew repairs **-1% every two
seconds** (same rate as yours), and once it drops back below **39%** the square goes
**red** again - meaning it can soak another 60% hit (39 + 60 = 99) and live. Between
39% and 50% it stays yellow (a little hysteresis so it doesn't flicker colour).

**Shooters.** About **1 in 4** aliens spawns with **7 torpedoes**. While it has
any, it is **frozen in place** - it never drifts, hunts or wanders, it only
shoots, and it can only shoot while its square is **on screen with you**. It
needs **two seconds** to "load up" after its square first comes on your screen,
then fires a **white tracer** at you no more than **once every two seconds** on
levels 1-2, **once a second** on level 3. Every shot is aimed fresh at wherever your ship is
*that instant*, then flies a **dead-straight line** - so a torpedo already in the
air can't correct, and shifting the ship forward or back after it's fired makes
it sail past. Out of torpedoes, the shooter stops holding position and **charges
straight at you to ram** - at **any** difficulty, level 1 included. Its tracers
are slower than yours - dodge them, or put the shield up.

What kills what:

| Contact | Result |
|---|---|
| Your torpedo hits an alien | Alien **+60%** damage; at 100% it flashes and is gone, else it's left wounded (yellow) |
| An alien runs into another alien | **Both** flash, then gone |
| An alien rams you, **shield up** | Alien is gone; shield **-20%** |
| An alien rams you, **shield down** | Alien is gone; hull **damage +40%** |
| An alien torpedo hits you, **shield up** | Torpedo stopped; shield **-1%** |
| An alien torpedo hits you, **shield down** | Hull **damage +10%** |

Hull damage at **100%**, **power at 0**, or the **countdown clock reaching
`00:00`** (a hard **15-minute** limit on every level) ends the run.

The **`Kills NN/MM` counter** (right of the gauge readouts) counts every alien
removed from the game, no matter how it died, out of the level's total (20 / 40
/ 60 for levels 1 / 2 / 3).

When the rocket is destroyed the screen shows `GAME OVER` and
`press any key to restart` - hit any key and you're back at the **start
screen** to pick a level for the next run (`~` still reboots to BOOTSEL for
reflashing instead).

**Winning.** On any level with aliens (1-3), destroy the whole `Kills NN/MM`
count and you get a full-screen **`YOU WON IN`** with your finish time in big
digits (time **taken**, counted up from `00:00`), a short victory jingle, then
`Press any key to continue` back to the start screen. Beat the clock, though -
run past **15:00** of play and it's `GAME OVER` regardless.

Fresh aliens are always spawned outside the visible screen, so one never just
pops into view next to you. The one exception: at difficulty **1-3** the game
starts with a single alien sitting at the **right edge of the box** - at a
random height, above or below your ship (never dead level, so you can't just
autopilot into it) - so you can see straight away what you're meant to shoot.
That first one is a **shooter**, but a deliberately **bad** ("rookie") one: its
first round sails about **20 pixels below** your ship and each round tightens up
until the **fifth**, from which point it (and every shot after) is aimed **dead
on**. Then it's out of torpedoes and **charges you to ram**. So a rookie left
alone *will* wear you down - it's a slow clock, not a free pass.

**Idle nudge.** Also at difficulty **1-3**: go **30 seconds without touching a
key** and the game intervenes. If you're still coasting it first **flip-and-burns
you to a stop** (you'll see the AUTOPILOT banner). Then, if a rookie is still
alive, it's handed **another 7 torpedoes** (so it keeps shooting - dead on by
now - instead of just ramming); if you'd killed it, a **fresh** rookie drops in
at the right edge. Only ever **one** rookie at a time. If the ship drifts far
enough that the rookie slides off the edge of the box, it's quietly removed.
Press anything and the 30-second timer resets. Sit idle long enough and the
hull damage from all this ends the game.

**Long Range Sensors.** When an alien is off the box but still lines up with it
on one axis - straight above, below, left, or right - a small red triangular
blip appears just inside that edge, pointing at it. An alien that's off
*diagonally* (so neither its X nor its Y overlaps the box) doesn't register;
nor does one that's on screen (you can already see it).

## Cloak (`C`)

Toggle the cloak with `C` (you need some power to switch it on). While cloaked:

- The **hull disappears** and the aliens **lose track of you** - any that were
  charging just keep drifting on the heading they had, and new ones can't lock
  on at all. **`CLOAKED`** shows in the readout column (bottom line).
- You **can't fire**, **can't raise shields**, and **thrust is capped at the
  slowest crawl** (the same speed the aliens move). Any speed you had bleeds
  down to that crawl.
- It **burns 2 power a second**, and drops on its own when power hits `0` - and
  power hitting 0 is game over, so don't stay cloaked to the last drop.

A blind alien can still blunder into you - cloak hides you, it doesn't make you
solid - and with no shields available that ram lands as a **+40% hull damage**
hit. Use the cloak to break away, not to sit still.

## Autopilot (`A` / `M`)

The game is normally in **Manual navigation** - you fly it. Press **`A`** to
turn on **Autopilot** - an `AUTOPILOT` banner appears in the box. Press `A`
again, or **`M`**, to go back to Manual (a brief `MANUAL` flash confirms it).

With Autopilot on, the four arrow keys stop being flight controls and each
become a **one-tap hop** - a fixed step of about one play-box (228 px):

1. The ship turns to point that way *on the screen* (`Up` = screen-up, etc.) -
   you see the side attitude jet firing as it swings round.
2. It fires the **main** engine twice to reach cruise speed, then coasts.
3. It fires the **front** (retro) engine only - never the main engine - to a
   dead stop **exactly one box away**, and snaps precisely onto that line, so
   tapping the same arrow repeatedly walks you in an exactly straight line.

Under the banner: `engaged` while a hop runs, otherwise (autopilot on, sitting
still between hops) the reminder `press J,K keys to rotate ship`. Your normal
flight keys are locked until a hop finishes (or you press `A` / `M`, or the fuel
runs out - then it just stops wherever it is and coasts). It is **not**
invulnerable: an alien can still reach you mid-hop - and if you see the hop is
about to fly you into one, **`Enter`** still works: it cancels the hop and flips
you to a retrograde stop.

Between hops, **`J`** and **`K`** hand-rotate the hull counter-clockwise and
clockwise (the arrow keys are busy). A hop costs roughly 10-20 fuel depending
on how far it has to turn first.

## Sound

The starter audio driver is a single square-wave voice per channel (100 Hz
minimum, no volume control). Four short sounds, highest priority wins the voice:

- **Alien destroyed** - a short, happy rising three-note chime, played the
  instant one of your torpedoes kills an alien. Beats every other sound.
- **Your fire** - a quick "pew", pitch dropping fast from high to low over about
  a tenth of a second.
- **Alien fire** - the same chirp **reversed**: pitch rising, low to high.
- **Thrusters** - a brief white-noise **hiss** (as close as a square voice
  gets: random high pitch every frame) on any frame a jet actually fires - a
  manual `Up` / `Down` / turn, a flip-and-burn, or an autopilot hop's turn and
  its accel/brake pulses (but not its silent coast) - trailing off about an
  eighth of a second after.

Plus a ~5-second **happy jingle**: once at program startup (over the splash
screen) and again on the `YOU WON IN` screen. It always plays start to finish
before input is read.

Everything else is silent.

Tune the pew with `PEW_HI` / `PEW_LO` / `PEW_MS`, the hiss with `HISS_LO` /
`HISS_HI` / `HISS_MS`, and the kill chime with `CHIME_N1` / `CHIME_N2` /
`CHIME_N3` / `CHIME_MS`, all in `space_game.h`.

## Screenshots (PicoCalc hardware, and the Windows build)

**On real hardware this feature is for the ClockworkPi PicoCalc and nothing
else.** It depends on the PicoCalc's exact LCD panel and its SD-card slot; on
any other board it is compiled out and does nothing. The Windows build has its
own version: `F5` writes the same kind of `SHOTxxxx.BMP` to the current folder.

On a PicoCalc, press **`F5`** and the current screen is saved to the SD card as
a randomly-named 24-bit BMP - `SHOT` followed by four hex digits, e.g.
`SHOT3A9F.BMP` - in the card's root directory. A one-line result flashes near
the top of the box for about two seconds (`Saved SHOT3A9F.BMP`, or `No SD card`
/ `BMP write failed` if something went wrong); the game keeps running
underneath.

It works by reading the LCD controller's frame memory back over SPI, which is a
PicoCalc-panel-specific trick - that is why it is PicoCalc-only. If a capture
ever comes out colour-swapped or inverted, flip `SHOT_FIX_SWAP_RB` /
`SHOT_FIX_INVERT` in `space_game.h` and rebuild.

The whole feature is **optional**. It is gated on the `PICOCALC` `#define` at
the top of `space_game.h` (on by default, because this game targets the
PicoCalc) and lives entirely in `space_game_screenshot.c` / `.h`. To build for
other hardware, `#undef PICOCALC` and delete those two files - see the header
comment in `space_game_screenshot.h` for the full recipe.

## Controls

| Key            | Action                                             |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Left / Right   | Rotate the ship in place (hold to keep turning) - fires a white attitude jet on the side opposite the turn, with a hiss. Orientation only - it does not bend your current course. Costs fuel by time spent turning (~5/sec), not per press; dead at 0 fuel |
| Up             | Fire the main engine - one shove along the nose per **distinct press** (holding it does nothing), added to your velocity, up to top speed. Coasts after; no drag. Costs 2 fuel per press; dead at 0 fuel |
| Down           | Mirror of `Up` - one shove per **distinct press** along the *opposite* of the nose, at **half** the strength. Not a brake; from a stop it flies you backwards. Costs 1 fuel per press; dead at 0 fuel |
| Space          | Fire a torpedo from the nose - one per press, max 20 on screen. Costs 1 ammo per shot; nothing at 0 ammo |
| S              | Raise the shield to 100% (costs 20 power; needs 20 power and no cloak). Press again to drop it. No timer - it only falls to hits (see Shield) |
| C              | Toggle the cloak (needs power). Hull vanishes, aliens lose you; but no firing, no shields, thrust capped at a crawl. Burns 2 power per second; drops at 0 power - and 0 power is game over |
| Enter          | Flip and burn - an autopilot that **always ends in a dead stop**, whatever your speed or heading: it swings the nose retrograde, then burns the main engine until velocity is zero. Needs fuel + speed. Steering/thrust/cloak locked out while it runs; the banner shows `AUTOPILOT` / `flip-and-burn`, then reverts to your mode when done. Takes time (an alien can hit you mid-flip) |
| ?              | Pause - freeze the game and show the `CONTROLS` legend until any key is pressed, then resume |
| A              | Toggle **Autopilot** (see below). A second `A` leaves it; aborts a hop in progress |
| M              | Leave Autopilot for **Manual navigation** (no-op if already manual). Flashes `MANUAL` |
| Arrows *(Autopilot)* | Each launches a one-box **hop** in that screen direction |
| J / K *(Autopilot)*  | Hand-rotate the hull counter-clockwise / clockwise, between hops |
| Esc            | Quit this game and go back to the start screen. Immediate, no prompt. On the `CONTROLS` screen it goes back to the start screen too |
| Q              | Quit - freezes the game and asks `Quit?`. Press `Y` to go back to the start screen (same as `Esc`, just with a confirm), any other key to cancel. Does **not** reboot |
| F5             | **PicoCalc only.** Save a screenshot of the screen to the SD card as a randomly-named 24-bit `SHOTxxxx.BMP` (needs a card inserted). Flashes the result for ~2 s and keeps playing. Compiled out on non-PicoCalc builds; not shown on the in-game `CONTROLS` legend |
| 0 / 1 / 2 / 3  | On the start screen - pick that difficulty and go |
| Any key        | `CONTROLS` screen - start the game now (skip the countdown). `GAME OVER` screen - back to the start screen |
| `~`            | Reboot into BOOTSEL (USB drive) mode for reflashing, from anywhere. `~` is Shift + backtick - the two-key combo is deliberate so a stray backtick can't drop you into BOOTSEL. Not shown on the in-game `CONTROLS` legend |

The keyboard is read straight from the PicoCalc south-bridge FIFO. Rotation
keys act while held (auto-repeat included); `Up`, `Down`, `Space`, `S`, `C`,
`A`, `M`, `Esc` and the Autopilot `Enter` all act on the **leading edge of a
press only** - the firmware's key-repeat while a key is held is ignored, so
each engine impulse is a deliberate tap.

## Building

Open the folder in VS Code with the Raspberry Pi Pico extension (Compile /
Run), or from a terminal with `PICO_SDK_PATH` set:

    cmake -B build -G Ninja
    ninja -C build

Output: `build/picocalc-space-game-<chip>.uf2` (`<chip>` is `RP2350` or `RP2040`, matching the board), which the build also copies to the
top-level folder as `picocalc-space-game-RP2350.uf2` or
`picocalc-space-game-RP2040.uf2` (depending on the board), so both chips'
builds can sit side by side. Flash it by copying to the `RPI-RP2` drive - hold
BOOTSEL on power-up, or press `~` in the app to drop back to BOOTSEL without
touching the board.

### On Windows

The same game also runs on a Windows PC through a small SDL2 layer in
[`desktop/`](desktop/) that stands in for the PicoCalc's LCD, keyboard and
audio drivers. From an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell with SDL2 installed:

    cmake -S desktop -B build-windows -G Ninja
    ninja -C build-windows

Output: `picocalc-space-game-Windows.exe` in the top-level folder. SDL2 is
linked statically, so it is a single file with no `SDL2.dll`. `~` closes the
program, and `F5` saves the screen as `SHOTxxxx.BMP` in the current folder
instead of on an SD card.

### Linux

The same source builds on Linux with the SDL2 development package installed
(for example `sudo apt install libsdl2-dev`). Unlike the Windows build, SDL2 is
**not** linked in statically: the program links `libSDL2` dynamically, and the
build copies that library next to the executable as `libSDL2-2.0.so.0`, where
the executable finds it through an `$ORIGIN` run-path. Keep the two files
together.

    cmake -S desktop -B build-linux
    cmake --build build-linux

Output: `picocalc-space-game-Linux` and `libSDL2-2.0.so.0` in the top-level folder.

The board is **not** pinned in `CMakeLists.txt` (the `set(PICO_BOARD ...)` line
is left commented out). Pick the target with the VS Code Pico extension's
"Switch Board", or pass `-DPICO_BOARD=pico` / `-DPICO_BOARD=pico2` to `cmake`.

### Smaller screens

The layout is all derived from `BOX_W` / `BOX_H` (the play box, 304 x 228) in
`space_game.h`, and the status strip is behind a `SHOW_STATUS` switch there (default on).
The box need not be square - X and Y each get their own `IN_HI_*` / `IN_SPAN_*`
/ `CENTRE_*`. To run on, say, a **240x240** panel: point the vendored LCD driver
at that panel, set `BOX_W` / `BOX_H` to fit, and set `SHOW_STATUS` to `0` - the
starfield then fills the screen
with no gauges. A compile-time assert stops you setting the box larger than the
panel. (The title / difficulty screens are laid out for a 320-wide panel; on a
narrower one their text just clips - shorten the strings if you care.) The
320x320 build is unchanged by any of this.

Porting to a non-PicoCalc panel, also `#undef PICOCALC` in `space_game.h` (or
just delete `space_game_screenshot.c` / `.h`): the `F5` screenshot reads the
LCD back over SPI in a way that is specific to the PicoCalc's panel, so it is
**PicoCalc-only** and must be compiled out everywhere else.

With `SHOW_STATUS 0` there are no gauges, so instead you get **low-resource
warnings down the right edge of the box**: `FUEL` / `PWR` / `AMMO` / `SHLD` go
**yellow under 20%** and **red under 10%** (shields only warn while actually
raised), and `HULL` goes **yellow over 70% damage**, **red over 85%**.

Suggested settings for other hardware (also noted in `space_game.h`'s comments):

| Target | `BOX_W` x `BOX_H` | `SHOW_STATUS` |
|---|---|---|
| Pimoroni PicoSystem (240x240) | 240 x 180 | `0` (panel too small for the gauges) |
| VGA 640x480 | 600 x 450 | `1` (gauges in the bottom strip) |

## Layout

The core is two files: **`space_game.h`** holds every constant *and every
declaration*, and **`space_game.c`** holds nothing but function bodies. An
optional third pair, **`space_game_screenshot.c`** / **`.h`**, adds the
PicoCalc-only `F5` screenshot and can be deleted outright (see that header's
comment).

| File                        | Purpose                                             |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `space_game.h`              | **Every `#define`** - the gameplay/layout tunables and the `RGB(...)` colour macros - plus the `PICOCALC` target-hardware switch, the `alien_t` struct, and every forward declaration for `space_game.c` (the `~45` helper prototypes), all behind an include guard. It pulls in `drivers/lcd.h` (for `RGB` / `WIDTH` / `HEIGHT`), so include it *after* the pico / driver headers. No function bodies live here. |
| `space_game.c`              | **All the game code, and only code.** `#include "space_game.h"`, then `main()` and `run_game()` (the whole playthrough) right at the top, then the helpers - no prototype block, since every declaration is in the header. A short summary comment sits at the very top; the full design write-up is in `GAME-DETAILS.txt`. |
| `GAME-DETAILS.txt`          | The long-form design reference - startup, the full control map, status, universe model, aliens, flight model, autopilot, rendering, audio. Prose only; nothing includes it. |
| `space_game_screenshot.c` / `.h` | **Optional, PicoCalc hardware only.** The `F5` screenshot - reads the LCD back over SPI and streams it to a BMP on the SD card. Entirely behind `#ifdef PICOCALC`; delete both files (and `#undef PICOCALC`) to build for any other board. |
| `CMakeLists.txt`            | Firmware build config - lists the starter driver `.c` files it compiles; copies the `.uf2` to the top level as `picocalc-space-game-RP2040.uf2` / `-RP2350.uf2`. |
| `desktop/`                  | Desktop (SDL2) build for Windows and Linux: its own `CMakeLists.txt` plus a small shim (`shim_*.c`, `pico/`, `hardware/`) that re-implements the starter driver API on SDL2, and `shim_screenshot.c`, the Windows stand-in for `F5`. Output `picocalc-space-game-Windows.exe`. |
| `pico_sdk_import.cmake`     | Standard Pico SDK bootstrap.                        |
| `picocalc-text-starter-main/` | Vendored copy of picocalc-text-starter (Blair Leduc). Read-only; only `drivers/lcd.c`, `drivers/southbridge.c`, `drivers/font-8x10.c` and `drivers/audio.c` (+ `audio.pio`) are built - plus `drivers/sdcard.c` / `drivers/fat32.c`, used only by the PicoCalc `F5` screenshot. |
| `CHANGELOG.md`              | Notable changes.                                    |

## Tuning

Everything adjustable lives in `space_game.h` as `#define`s:

- **Box:** `BOX_W`, `BOX_H`, `BORDER`, `COL_BORDER`.
- **Motion:** `THRUST_IMPULSE` (shove per `Up`, along the nose), `BRAKE_IMPULSE`
  (shove per `Down`, opposite the nose; defaults to half `THRUST_IMPULSE`),
  `SPEED_MAX` (hard speed cap, also the nearest star's px/frame), `ROT_STEP`.
- **Flip and burn (`Enter`):** `FNB_ROT_STEP` (flip turn rate, defaults to
  `ROT_STEP`), `FNB_BURN_FRAMES` (burn length after the flip), `FNB_MIN_SPEED`
  (won't start below this speed).
- **Autopilot (`A` / `M`):** `AUTO_DIST` (hop distance - defaults to `BOX_H`,
  about one play-box), `AUTO_CRUISE` (hop cruise speed - defaults to two
  `THRUST_IMPULSE` pulses), `AUTO_TXT_COL` / `AUTO_TXT_ROW` (the one autopilot
  banner - also used by the flip-and-burn), `MANUAL_TXT_MS` (how long `MANUAL`
  flashes on exit).
- **Starfield:** `STAR_COUNT`, `DEPTH_MIN` (how slow/dim the farthest stars
  are), `STAR_LUM_MIN`, `STAR_FAR_TINT`.
- **Streaks:** `STREAK_MIN` (speed at which stars start to streak), `STREAK_GAIN`
  (streak length vs. speed), `STREAK_MAX` (longest streak).
- **Ship:** `SHIP_NOSE` / `SHIP_TAIL` / `SHIP_HALF`.
- **Main flame:** `FLAME_HOLD_MS` (how long it stays lit after `Up`, ~0.5 s),
  `FLAME_HALF`, `FLAME_LEN`, `FLAME_FLICKER`, `FLAME_COL`.
- **Front flames** (`Down`): `BRAKE_HOLD_MS`, `BRAKE_OFF_X` / `BRAKE_OFF_Y`
  (where they sit), `BRAKE_HALF`, `BRAKE_LEN`, `COL_BRAKE`.
- **Attitude jet** (`Left`/`Right`): `RCS_OFF_X` / `RCS_OFF_Y` (where the jet
  base sits on the hull side), `RCS_HALF` (base height), `RCS_LEN` (how far it
  sticks out); shares `COL_BRAKE`.
- **Torpedoes:** `MAX_TORPEDOES`, `TORPEDO_SPEED` (keep it above `SPEED_MAX`),
  `TORPEDO_LEN`, `COL_TORPEDO`.
- **Alien torpedoes:** `ALIEN_SHOOTER_EVERY` (1-in-N aliens shoot), `ALIEN_TORPEDOES`
  (clip size), `ALIEN_TORPEDO_MAX` (array), `ATORPEDO_SPEED`, `ALIEN_FIRE_MS`
  (min ms between shots - doubled at levels 1-2), `ALIEN_ARM_MS` (load-up delay after first coming into
  view), `ALIEN_ROOKIE_MISS` (px a rookie's 1st shot aims low) / `ALIEN_ROOKIE_SHOTS`
  (shot by which the miss has shrunk to 0 - dead on after),
  `IDLE_ROOKIE_MS` (levels 1-3: ms of no keypress before the ship is stopped and
  a rookie spawned / reloaded), `COL_ATORPEDO`.
- **Shield:** `SHIELD_R` (ring size), `SHIELD_START` (level when raised),
  `SHIELD_PWR_COST` (power to raise), `SHIELD_HIT_TORPEDO` / `SHIELD_HIT_RAM`
  (level lost per torpedo / ram), `COL_SHIELD` (hull/ring), `COL_GAUGE_SHIELD`
  (bar).
- **Hull damage:** `SHIP_DMG_TORPEDO` (10, per alien torpedo with the shield
  down), `SHIP_DMG_RAM` (40, per ram with the shield down), `DMG_REPAIR_STEP`
  (1, mended per tick) / `DMG_REPAIR_MS` (2000, ms between ticks), `SHIP_WOUND_ON`
  (33 - hull draws `COL_SHIP_WOUND` yellow once damage is above this *or* power
  is below this percent), `DMG_MAX` (100 = destroyed). Power reaching 0 is also
  game over.
- **Alien damage:** `ALIEN_HIT_DMG` (60, per player torpedo), `ALIEN_DMG_MAX`
  (100 = destroyed, so two hits), `ALIEN_WOUND_ON` (> 50% -> yellow),
  `ALIEN_WOUND_OFF` (< 39% -> back to red), `COL_ALIEN_WOUND`. Heals at
  `DMG_REPAIR_STEP` / `DMG_REPAIR_MS`, same as the hull.
- **Cloak:** `CLOAK_DRAIN` (power spent per `CLOAK_DRAIN_MS` while cloaked);
  the crawl cap is `BRAKE_IMPULSE`.
- **Aliens:** `alien_max` (total ever spawned = the score's "/max"),
  `alien_speed` (the *default* px/frame each alien gets at spawn - individual
  aliens carry their own `alien_t.speed`, so a difficulty can mix fast and slow
  ones), `alien_spawn_max` (far spawn distance) and `alien_ram_and_fire` (bool,
  default `false` - lets a loaded alien move/ram while still shooting) are
  **runtime variables** in `space_game.c`. `run_game()` sets `alien_max` from the
  level - `ALIEN_MAX_L1` (20) / `ALIEN_MAX_L2` (40) / `ALIEN_MAX_L3` (60), or
  `ALIEN_MAX_INIT` (50) for level 0; `alien_speed` / `alien_spawn_max` keep their
  `*_INIT` starts. Still `#define`s: `ALIEN_ONSCREEN` (how many in play at
  once), `ALIEN_SIZE`, `ALIEN_SPAWN_MIN` (near spawn distance),
  `ALIEN_INTRO_X` (px right of centre for the level-1-3
  starting target) / `ALIEN_INTRO_YMIN` / `ALIEN_INTRO_YMAX` (its random height
  band off centre), `ALIEN_CULL_DIST` (unseen drifter recycled past
  this), `SPOT_PAUSE` (freeze frames on spotting you), `ALIEN_FLASH`
  (hit-flash frames), `GAMEOVER_FLASH` (rocket death-flash frames),
  `LRS_LEN` / `LRS_HALF` (Long Range Sensors blip size), `COL_ALIEN` /
  `COL_ALIEN_WOUND` / `COL_ALIEN_FLASH` / `COL_SHIP_FLASH`.
- **Fuel / ammo / power:** `FUEL_MAX`, `FUEL_COST_FWD` (per `Up`),
  `FUEL_COST_REV` (per `Down`), `FUEL_ROT_FRAMES` (frames of turning per -1
  fuel), `AMMO_MAX`, `POWER_MAX`.
- **Status-strip layout:** `STATUS_BY` (below-strip top - `BOX_H` rounded up to end in 9 so
  the readouts land on the 10px glyph grid); `GAUGE_X` / `GAUGE_W` / `GAUGE_H` (also the
  stack pitch, so the five bars touch) + `GAUGE_TXT_COL`, in order
  `FUEL_GAUGE_Y` / `FUEL_TXT_ROW`, `PWR_GAUGE_Y` / `PWR_TXT_ROW`,
  `AMMO_GAUGE_Y` / `AMMO_TXT_ROW`, `SHIELD_GAUGE_Y` / `SHIELD_GTXT_ROW`,
  `DMG_GAUGE_Y` / `DMG_GTXT_ROW` (fuel/power/shield/damage print `nn%`, ammo
  prints the count); `KILLS_TXT_COL` with `LVL_TXT_ROW` (`Lv N`) /
  `CLOCK_TXT_COL` + `CLOCK_TXT_ROW` + `GAME_LEN_S` (900 - the `MM:SS` clock
  counts this down from 15:00; 00:00 = GAME OVER) /
  `SCORE_VAL_ROW` (`Kills` or `No Aliens`) / `CLK_TXT_COL` + `CLK_TXT_ROW`
  (cloak `CLOAKED`), `UNIV_TXT_COL` / `UNIV_TXT_ROW` (coordinate readout),
  `GO_TXT_COL` / `GO_TXT_ROW` ("GAME OVER") + `GO_MSG_COL` / `GO_MSG_ROW`
  (restart prompt) - all four now `BOX_W`/`BOX_H`-derived so they centre in the
  box; `QUIT_TXT_COL` / `QUIT_TXT_ROW` (`Q` quit confirmation).
- **Win screen:** `WIN_SCALE_TXT` / `WIN_SCALE_CLK` / `WIN_L1_*` / `WIN_L2_*` /
  `WIN_MSG_*` / `WIN_SONG_MS` (the `YOU WON IN` card).
- **Hints (levels 0-1):** `COL_HINT` (grey), `HINT_MS` (2000, on-screen time),
  `HINT_FIRE_AFTER_MS` (30000, delay before the "SPACE key to fire" nag),
  `HINT_Q_AT_1_MS` / `HINT_Q_AT_2_MS` (60000 / 120000, the level-0 "Press Q to
  Quit" marks), `HINT_TXT_SCALE` / `HINT_TXT_Y` / `HINT_NA_TXT_X` /
  `HINT_S_TXT_X` / `HINT_FIRE_TXT_X` / `HINT_MOVE_TXT_X` / `HINT_Q_TXT_X` (the
  five captions), `HINT_ARROW_TIP` / `HINT_ARROW_BACK` / `HINT_ARROW_HALF` (the
  grey "next alien" triangle).
- **Universe:** `UNIVERSE_SIZE` (pixels per axis; `UNIVERSE_HALF` is the
  start point).
- **Status-strip colours:** `COL_GAUGE_FRAME` / `COL_GAUGE_DRAIN` (shared) and
  `COL_GAUGE_FUEL` / `COL_GAUGE_AMMO` / `COL_GAUGE_POWER` / `COL_GAUGE_SHIELD` /
  `COL_GAUGE_DMG` / `COL_STATUS_TXT`; `COL_WARN_LOW` / `COL_WARN_CRIT` and
  `WARN_TXT_COL` / `WARN_TXT_ROW0` for the `SHOW_STATUS 0` right-edge warnings.
- **Loop & audio:** `FRAME_MS`; `PEW_HI` / `PEW_LO` / `PEW_MS` (firing chirp -
  the alien one is the same values, swept the other way); `HISS_LO` / `HISS_HI`
  / `HISS_MS` (thruster/turn white-noise hiss); `CHIME_N1` / `CHIME_N2` /
  `CHIME_N3` / `CHIME_MS` (the "alien destroyed" chime - three note pitches and
  the total length).
- **F5 screenshot (PicoCalc only, inside the `#ifdef PICOCALC` block):**
  `SHOT_READ_HZ` (SPI clock for reading the frame memory back), `SHOT_NAME_FMT`
  (BMP filename pattern), `SHOT_MSG_MS` / `SHOT_MSG_COL` / `SHOT_MSG_ROW` (the
  on-screen result line), `SHOT_FIX_SWAP_RB` / `SHOT_FIX_INVERT` (correct a
  colour-swapped or inverted capture). The whole block only exists when
  `PICOCALC` is defined.
